variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: An AI gateway is a trusted service boundary between an application and one or more model-serving APIs. It authenticates the caller, binds the request to a tenant, applies policy and budget controls, chooses an eligible route, invokes a provider-specific adapter, and records what happened.
variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Ownership by layer”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Application
pairs.detail: Owns the user experience, conversation state, product deadline, and downstream handling of a partial or canceled stream.
pairs.explanation: Owns the user experience, conversation state, product deadline, and downstream handling of a partial or canceled stream.

pairs.label: Gateway
pairs.detail: Owns trusted identity, tenant policy, quota, budget, route eligibility, release policy, audit evidence, and failure containment.
pairs.explanation: Owns trusted identity, tenant policy, quota, budget, route eligibility, release policy, audit evidence, and failure containment.

pairs.label: Adapter
pairs.detail: Owns native request mapping, SDK use, error classification, cancellation behavior, stream parsing, and usage normalization for one API.
pairs.explanation: Owns native request mapping, SDK use, error classification, cancellation behavior, stream parsing, and usage normalization for one API.

pairs.label: Provider
pairs.detail: Owns the served model, platform limits, native safety mechanisms, billing semantics, and the actual completion or failure.
pairs.explanation: Owns the served model, platform limits, native safety mechanisms, billing semantics, and the actual completion or failure.

variants.hint: Give each part the one job only it can do, then rule out the rest. This boundary matters because model calls carry more than text.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Application: Owns the user experience, conversation state, product deadline, and downstream handling of a partial or canceled stream. Gateway: Owns trusted identity, tenant policy, quota, budget, route eligibility, release policy, audit evidence, and failure containment. Adapter: Owns native request mapping, SDK use, error classification, cancellation behavior, stream parsing, and usage normalization for one API. Provider: Owns the served model, platform limits, native safety mechanisms, billing semantics, and the actual completion or failure.

pairs.explanation: Verify the caller, derive tenant and plan from trusted identity data, and attach allowed data classes, regions, and policy version.

pairs.explanation: Create a product-level envelope with task type, input blocks, required capabilities, output limit, deadline, and cancellation signal.

pairs.label: Filter routes

pairs.explanation: Reject candidates that violate capability, context, tenant, safety, residency, health, quota, budget, or deadline constraints.

pairs.label: Rank and invoke
pairs.detail: Score only eligible candidates, obtain the chosen adapter's credential just in time, invoke it, and preserve native response semantics.
pairs.explanation: Score only eligible candidates, obtain the chosen adapter's credential just in time, invoke it, and preserve native response semantics.

variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: An AI gateway is a trusted service boundary between an application and one or more model-serving APIs. It authenticates the caller, binds the request to a tenant, applies policy and budget controls, chooses an eligible route, invokes a provider-specific adapter, and records what happened.
variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Distinguish two cache mechanisms”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Provider prompt cache
pairs.detail: The provider may reuse encoded prompt prefixes.
pairs.explanation: The provider may reuse encoded prompt prefixes. Its keying, lifetime, quota effect, token fields, and price are provider-specific. The gateway records the native outcome but does not pretend it is portable.

pairs.label: Gateway response cache
pairs.detail: A stored model response can bypass inference.
pairs.explanation: A stored model response can bypass inference. Its key must include tenant scope, normalized input, model and adapter version, tool set, safety policy, response format, and freshness rules. Sensitive or personalized tasks often should not use it.

variants.hint: Give each part the one job only it can do, then rule out the rest. This boundary matters because model calls carry more than text.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Provider prompt cache: The provider may reuse encoded prompt prefixes. Gateway response cache: A stored model response can bypass inference.

variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: An AI gateway is a trusted service boundary between an application and one or more model-serving APIs. It authenticates the caller, binds the request to a tenant, applies policy and budget controls, chooses an eligible route, invokes a provider-specific adapter, and records what happened.
variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Roll out routing policy with evaluation evidence”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Evaluate offline
pairs.detail: Run task-specific and safety suites by tenant class, language, input length, tool use, and expected fallback route.
pairs.explanation: Run task-specific and safety suites by tenant class, language, input length, tool use, and expected fallback route. Compare against a pinned control.

pairs.label: Shadow safely
pairs.detail: Where policy permits, compute route decisions without serving the candidate response.
pairs.explanation: Where policy permits, compute route decisions without serving the candidate response. Avoid duplicating restricted data or billable inference merely to create telemetry.

pairs.label: Canary by cohort
pairs.explanation: Expose a small, reversible share. Keep the stable policy live and cap retry amplification, fallback share, cost, safety failures, and quality regression.

pairs.label: Expand or roll back
pairs.detail: Expand only after minimum evidence passes.
pairs.explanation: Expand only after minimum evidence passes. Automatically stop or roll back on hard policy, safety, quality, or circuit-breaker gates.
